# vvm_vm (Resource)

A VVM virtual machine (`/v1/vms`).

`terraform apply` returns when the control plane reports the VM `Running` — scheduled onto a host, its disk made from the golden image, its network reconciled and booted. It does not return when the API merely accepted the create. On timeout the error carries the state the control plane last reported and the state of the scheduling job, so a VM that could not be placed says so.

Every attribute is immutable: a change destroys and recreates. Power and resize are day-2 operations, done through the API or the Ansible collection, not by editing this resource.

⚠️ There is no DHCP. On a VSI cluster the control plane assigns the guest's address at create and it is reported in `guest_ipv4`; nothing else will tell you what it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "vvm_vm" "app" {
  cluster_id          = var.cluster_id
  datastore_id        = vvm_datastore.app.id
  network_id          = vvm_network.app.id
  name                = "app-vm"
  vcpu_request        = 2
  memory_request_mib  = 4096
  golden_image        = var.golden_image
  boot_disk_gib       = 20
  boot_subnet_id      = var.boot_subnet_id
  ssh_authorized_keys = [var.ssh_public_key]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `boot_disk_gib` (Number) Size of the boot disk, in GiB.
- `boot_subnet_id` (String) Id of the VPC subnet the VM's NIC attaches to.
- `cluster_id` (String) UUID of the cluster the VM runs on.
- `datastore_id` (String) UUID of the datastore the VM's disks live on — reference a `vvm_datastore`. It must belong to `cluster_id`.
- `golden_image` (String) Stem of the golden image on the datastore, WITHOUT an extension: the host resolves `ubuntu-2404` to `<images>/ubuntu-2404.qcow2`. A value carrying `.qcow2`, a path separator or a leading dot is refused.
- `memory_request_mib` (Number) Memory the scheduler must find room for, in MiB.
- `name` (String) Name of the VM.
- `network_id` (String) UUID of the guest network the VM attaches to — reference a `vvm_network`. It must belong to `cluster_id`, and a network that is being deleted is refused.
- `vcpu_request` (Number) vCPUs the scheduler must find room for.

### Optional

- `create_timeout` (String) How long `terraform apply` waits for this resource to reach its target state, as a Go duration (e.g. `45m`). Default `45m`. On timeout the error carries the state the control plane last reported and the state of the job behind it.
- `delete_timeout` (String) How long `terraform destroy` waits for this resource to be gone, as a Go duration. Default `30m`.
- `dr_tier` (String) DR tier. ⛔ Only `none` is accepted today — VVM replicates no VM to another region, so the control plane refuses any other tier rather than record protection that does not exist.
- `encrypted` (Boolean) Encrypt the boot disk under the project's Key Protect root key. Refused when the control plane has no Key Protect instance configured, rather than accepted and silently stored as a plain disk.
- `hostname` (String) cloud-init hostname for the guest.
- `ssh_authorized_keys` (List of String) Public keys cloud-init installs in the guest. Keys that would reach no user who can log in are refused at create.
- `user_data` (String, Sensitive) cloud-init user-data, handed to the guest verbatim, e.g. `file("cloud-init/web.yaml")`.

### Read-Only

- `actual_state` (String) The state the control plane has OBSERVED, reconciled against reality. `terraform plan` shows a change here when the VM was changed outside Terraform.
- `current_host_id` (String) The host the VM is OBSERVED on. Null until the scheduler places it. A VM migrated out of band shows up here on the next plan.
- `desired_state` (String) The state the control plane is working towards.
- `guest_ipv4` (String) The guest's address, assigned by the control plane on a VSI cluster. Empty on bare metal, where the guest takes its address from the network itself.
- `id` (String) UUID the control plane minted for this VM.
- `job_id` (String) The asynchronous job the create emitted. Named in the error when a create or a delete runs out of time, so the real job state is what the operator sees.
- `updated_at` (String) When the row last changed, as the API reported it. Used as the `If-Match` precondition on a delete; it is re-read immediately before the delete is sent, because the row's timestamp moves on its own.
